title: Titanium Femoral Condyle
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-7Nb (ASTM F1295) is selected as Ni-free alternative for this orthopedic joints implant, replacing V with Nb to eliminate cytotoxicity while maintaining 900 MPa tensile equivalent to Ti-6Al-4V. This rationale is driven by total knee femoral condyle component (ti-6al-7nb) and service environment demands.
process: CNC swiss turning for orthopedic joints geometry
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish
commonFailures: Fe contamination from machining - requires acid passivation 20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C per ASTM F86

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Femoral Condyle suitable for Total knee femoral condyle component (Ti-6Al-7Nb)?
faq.a: Titanium Femoral Condyle uses Ti-6Al-7Nb because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address orthopedic joints operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Femoral Condyle?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Femoral Condyle require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. orthopedic joints components receive Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Femoral Condyle shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Knee implant / Femoral component orthopedic joints components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
